hints: Notice the $230 \text{ W}$ is the wasted power, not the input power, and with $74\%$ efficiency the wasted fraction is $100\% - 74\% = 26\%$.
Connect efficiency to powers using $\text{efficiency} = P_{useful}/P_{input}$ and $P_{input} = P_{useful} + P_{wasted}$.
First find $P_{input}$ from $0.26 \times P_{input} = 230 \text{ W}$, then find $P_{useful} = 0.74 \times P_{input}$.
walkthrough: Identify the wasted fraction. Efficiency $74\%$ means $74\%$ of input is useful, so $100\% - 74\% = 26\% = 0.26$ of input is wasted.
Use the wasted power to find total input power. $0.26 \times P_{input} = 230 \text{ W}$, so $P_{input} = 230/0.26 \text{ W}$.
Calculate the input: $P_{input} \approx 884.6 \text{ W}$, about $880 \text{ W}$ with the given data.
Find useful output from efficiency: $P_{useful} = 0.74 \times P_{input} = 0.74 \times 884.6 \text{ W}$.
Calculate the useful power: $P_{useful} \approx 654.6 \text{ W}$, which to two significant figures is about $650 \text{ W}$. This is option C.

options.A: This is $0.74 \times 230 \text{ W} \approx 170 \text{ W}$. It wrongly treats the $230 \text{ W}$ of wasted power as the total input power.
options.B: This is $230 \text{ W} / 0.74 \approx 310 \text{ W}$. It wrongly treats the $230 \text{ W}$ of wasted power as the useful output power.
options.C: Wasted power is $26\%$ of input, so input is $230/0.26$ and useful power is $0.74$ of that, about $650 \text{ W}$.
options.D: This is $230 \text{ W} / 0.26 \approx 880 \text{ W}$. This is the total input power, not the useful output power.
